key_insight: Normalize and optimize policy updates separately for each reward group so heterogeneous or conflicting rewards no longer dominate or interfere with each other; this yields more stable and effective multi-reward RL training. GDPO decouples reward-group normalization from the aggregated policy update, preserving per-preference signal while enabling a unified policy.
problem_solved: Standard multi-reward pipelines (often using GRPO) suffer from scale imbalance and reward interference: large or noisy reward signals can dominate updates, leading to unstable training and poor trade-offs across preferences. The paper addresses how to reliably optimize a single policy under multiple, diverse reward objectives.
method: Group-wise normalization: compute normalization (e.g., advantage or gradient scaling) independently for each reward group to remove scale differences and stabilize per-group learning signals.
Decoupled policy updates: form per-group update directions or trust-region adjustments and combine them into a single aggregated policy update that preserves each group's contribution.
Practical integration: design the aggregation/weighting so it is compatible with common policy optimization frameworks (PPO/GRPO-style pipelines) while avoiding cross-group domination.
impact: GDPO enables practitioners to train a single policy that better balances multiple human preferences or reward objectives, improving stability and alignment in multi-reward RL settings without extensive reward engineering. It’s a practical plug-in for RLHF and multi-objective RL workflows.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: GRPO vs GDPO showing single global normalization (GRPO) vs per-group normalization and decoupled aggregation (GDPO).
Multi-metric radar or bar chart: performance across several reward criteria before and after GDPO to show improved balance.
Flow diagram: data → per-group advantage computation & normalization → per-group update → aggregation → policy update.
Icon set: multiple reward icons (e.g., safety, helpfulness, style) feeding into separate normalization blocks to illustrate decoupling.
paper_title: GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL Optimization
paper_authors: Shih-Yang Liu, Xin Dong, Ximing Lu, Shizhe Diao, Peter Belcak
